selection_criteria: Official code exists, so the hidden reference can be compared afterward
A CPU run finishes in under 30 minutes on a laptop
At least one numeric claim in a table
The code's license allows running it
note: The v0.1 gate needs three; five light papers are registered here (vision + text) so the set has margin. Claim values are pinned per study at build time, not stored here. Three of the five (Fashion-MNIST, KMNIST, MNIST-1D) have already been reproduced end to end.

papers.title: Fashion-MNIST: a Novel Image Dataset for Benchmarking Machine Learning Algorithms
papers.claim_location: Benchmark table (benchmark_table.tex) — scikit-learn classifier accuracies, e.g. GaussianNB, DecisionTreeClassifier, RandomForestClassifier rows
papers.why_chosen: Official sklearn benchmark scripts exist; deterministic tree/NB baselines; runs in minutes on CPU; clear numeric table. Already reproduced.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Classical Japanese Literature (Kuzushiji-MNIST)
papers.claim_location: Table 1 — 4-Nearest-Neighbour baseline accuracies (MNIST and Kuzushiji-MNIST columns)
papers.why_chosen: Deterministic 4-NN baseline, no training; official baseline code; runs in minutes on CPU. Already reproduced.

papers.title: Scaling Down Deep Learning with MNIST-1D
papers.claim_location: Section 'Classification' / Table 1 — logistic, MLP, GRU, CNN test accuracies
papers.why_chosen: Fixed public dataset; paper states experiments take ~10 min on CPU; clear table. Logistic-regression claim already reproduced; MLP/CNN are the stretch.

papers.title: Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification (fastText)
papers.claim_location: Table 1 — test accuracy on text-classification datasets (AG News, DBpedia, Yelp, etc.)
papers.why_chosen: fastText is designed for CPU and trains in minutes; official MIT code; well-defined accuracy table. Adds an NLP paper to a vision-heavy set.

papers.title: Cold Case: The Lost MNIST Digits (QMNIST)
papers.claim_location: Test error/accuracy table on the reconstructed MNIST test set (kNN / SVM / MLP baselines)
papers.why_chosen: Official reconstruction code; CPU-light kNN baseline; a numeric error table; a different flavour of reproduction (dataset reconstruction).
